Dear Dr. Bennett,

Thank you for agreeing to see this 22-year-old gentleman for comprehensive clinical evaluation. He attends our clinic accompanied by his parents, who provide full-time care. Because of a profound global cognitive impairment, he remains completely non-verbal and dependent for all basic activities of daily living. 

On physical examination, his occipitofrontal circumference is remarkably small at 49.5 cm, placing him far below the 3rd percentile. He presents with distinctly coarsened facial morphology, including a wide nasal bridge and thickened, prominent lips. Examination of the perineum reveals atypical external genitalia characterized by penoscrotal transposition and bifid scrotal folds. Notably, his stretched penile length is well within the normal adult distribution with no evidence of an abnormally small phallus, and both gonads are fully descended bilaterally with no testicular retention.

Cardiovascular investigations have documented a congenital two-leaflet aortic valve accompanied by a discrete thoracic aortic narrowing. His past medical history is also significant for a high-grade osteogenic sarcoma of the distal femur diagnosed two years ago, which was managed with limb-sparing resection; ongoing surveillance imaging remains completely clear. Routine laboratory studies show a reduced hemoglobin alongside a depressed mean corpuscular volume, while his ferritin, platelets, and white cell count are normal. Renal and hepatic panels are entirely unremarkable, and he takes only daily vitamin D. Family history is negative for congenital anomalies or early-onset malignancies.

Given this constellation of findings, I would greatly value your specialized assessment regarding appropriate investigations and longitudinal care.

Warm regards,

Dr. Julian Ward
Department of Internal Medicine
